solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: New wine Her Majesty's put by for inspection

indicators.note: placed beside, so the royal letters are set alongside the wine

parts.note: must is unfermented or partly fermented grape juice
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen; the 's is the verb 'has' joining the pieces

explanation.surface: A cask of young wine belonging to the Queen is set aside to be checked by an inspector.
explanation.definitionFit: A muster is an assembly of troops for inspection, as in 'pass muster', so the word stands for the inspection itself.

clue.text: Confession — food thrown over copper by secretary

indicators.note: next to, so the assistant comes alongside
draped around, so the food encloses the metal

parts.note: a meal is food
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a PA, personal assistant, is a secretary

explanation.surface: A secretary owns up to tipping food over a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman but is the metal's chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase, 'my fault', is an admission of guilt, a confession.

clue.text: Struggle to get started

definitions.meaning: the phrasal verb meaning to begin work energetically

explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a brief fight, and to set to is to start working with vigour.

clue.text: Rhubarb lotion

definitions.meaning: British slang for nonsense or meaningless talk
a liquid for bathing a sore eye

explanation.definitionFit: The word means nonsense, like rhubarb in British slang, and also a soothing liquid for the eyes.

clue.text: Marsupial's credible (but brief) expression of doubt

indicators.note: cut short, so only the opening of the word for credible is kept, as in the colloquial 'poss'

parts.note: something credible is possible
um is a hesitant noise of doubt

explanation.surface: An animal seems to voice a short, hesitant 'possibly' as if unsure of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' trims POSSIBLE to the informal POSS.
explanation.definitionFit: The possum is an Australasian or American pouched mammal, an example of a marsupial.

clue.text: Firm up part of oratorio to include new instrument

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: to contain, so the song takes in the letter for new

parts.note: an aria is a solo song forming part of an oratorio

explanation.surface: A choir management firm wants a fresh instrument in its oratorio.
explanation.definitionFit: This small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Left inside, squander the Telegraph's brilliance

indicators.note: within, so the letter for left goes into the word for squander

parts.note: to squander money is to spend it
the clue is in the Telegraph, so the paper's own is 'our'

explanation.surface: Wasting money inside the Telegraph undermines the newspaper's brilliance.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendour is magnificence or great brightness, a synonym of brilliance.

clue.text: Note part way through brooding solo

indicators.note: set partway into, so the note letter sits inside the word for brooding

parts.note: brooding means sullen or moody

explanation.surface: A musician sounds a note midway through a gloomy solo piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A monody is a song or ode for a single voice, hence a solo.

clue.text: Keep pace?

definitions.meaning: a keep is a castle's stronghold, a secure place
pace as speed, the quality of being quick

explanation.surface: A runner's coach urges someone to keep up with the others.
explanation.definitionFit: A stronghold is a fortress or keep, and the abstract noun for quickness is a synonym of pace.

clue.text: Cut bits of plant on saucer, resulting in injury

parts.note: to slip a plant is to take cuttings from it
a saucer is flat and round, like a disc

explanation.surface: A gardener takes cuttings over a saucer and hurts themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A displaced spinal cartilage causing back pain is a common back injury.

clue.text: Dispatching missing millions is invalid

indicators.note: without, so the letter for millions is lost from the word for dispatching

parts.note: dispatching letters is mailing them
M is the standard abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: Sending out post while a huge sum has gone missing is not legally valid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invalid' here is the adjective meaning unwell, not 'not valid'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is unwell or sickly, an invalid in the adjectival sense, is poorly or sick.

clue.text: Game licence update delivered, Oliver heads for employment

indicators.note: the leading letters of the four words are the ones to put to use

explanation.surface: A man called Oliver receives a new driving licence and heads off to start a job.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a simple board game of dice and counters, a children's pastime.

clue.text: Coo! If Diana performs, I'm a fan!

indicators.note: the letters of the exclamation and name act out a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An admirer gasps with delight at the prospect of Princess Diana putting on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: An enthusiast or devotee of something would say they are a keen follower, which is what the exclamation claims.

clue.text: Honest and quiet player

parts.note: an honest person is upright
piano is the musical direction for playing softly

explanation.surface: A sportsperson or performer is described as decent and reserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'player' looks like a person but is a musical instrument that plays.
explanation.definitionFit: This vertical-strung keyboard instrument is something that plays music, a player in an extended sense.

clue.text: Undercover work?

parts.note: an undercover agent works on the inside
a job is a piece of work

explanation.surface: A question about whether something is secret spy work.
explanation.definitionFit: A crime committed by someone within the organisation is secret work done from within.

clue.text: My Parisian bird — rat-slayer extraordinaire?

parts.note: mon is French for my
a goose is a bird

explanation.surface: A French speaker boasts that their pet bird is a champion killer of rats.
explanation.definitionFit: This small carnivore is famed for killing snakes and rats, a superb vermin hunter.

clue.text: Surrogate husband's going into space

parts.note: a surrogate is a stand-in or substitute
a groom is a newly married husband; the 's is 'is' joining the pieces

explanation.surface: A substitute husband is being launched into outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase means room for spectators who have no seats, a kind of space in a venue.

clue.text: A handy girl to call up — but lacking 'bottom'?

parts.note: handy means close by

indicators.note: in a down clue, being called up means the letters rise and so are read backwards

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A useful young woman to phone, though perhaps lacking substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom' in quotes is the old sense of solid character, but here a literal bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Abyssal describes the ocean depths so deep they seem bottomless, like an abyss.

clue.text: One's possibly to make a discovery?

parts.note: the first word of the phrase rearranges the letters of the word, and the second word is a signal for that rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone muses about whether they are likely to find something.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the phrase as wordplay: its first word jumbles 'one's' and 'out' signals the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To sniff out or detect something is to find it, to make a discovery.

clue.text: Being of a high order, and special, is given initial honour — about time

indicators.note: around, so the special letters surround the period of time

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: the first letter of the word honour is taken

explanation.surface: A distinguished person is given an honour at last after a long wait.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraph is an angel of the highest rank in the celestial hierarchy.

clue.text: Sadly, end is down to fatal errors

indicators.note: knocked down, so the letters of the three words fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A mournful remark that a death was caused by mistakes that proved fatal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'down' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The seven sins of Christian teaching that bring spiritual death are mortal transgressions, hence fatal errors.

clue.text: Riotous time at Cambridge, perhaps? It's saucy, too!

parts.note: rag week is a student festival of pranks and fundraising at British universities
U stands for university, Cambridge being an example

explanation.surface: A cheeky exclamation about student high jinks at Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes a student rag at Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragu is an Italian meat sauce, so it is a saucy thing in the literal sense.

clue.text: Brief cotton regularly appearing in Page 3, perhaps?

indicators.note: every other letter is taken, here the even ones

explanation.surface: Skimpy cotton underwear on a tabloid's Page 3 model.
explanation.walkthrough: Page 3 of The Sun was notorious for topless models; here it is just an odd page.
explanation.definitionFit: A recto is a right-hand page of a book, always odd-numbered, so page three is one.

clue.text: Instruments made from curious jawbones we dug out

indicators.note: strange, so the remaining letters come out in an odd order
removed, so the letters of the little word are excavated from the bones

explanation.surface: Musical instruments are fashioned from strange jaw bones that an archaeologist excavated.
explanation.definitionFit: These stringed folk instruments with round bodies are examples of musical instruments.

clue.text: Hack doubly in hurry

indicators.note: twice over, so the word for hack is written two times

parts.note: to hack is to chop

explanation.surface: A journalist rushes, filing twice as fast.
explanation.definitionFit: This exclamation urges someone to move quickly, a call to hurry up.

clue.text: Totter throwing books into pit

indicators.note: tossing, so the volumes are cast inside the hollow
places the volumes inside the hollow

parts.note: a pit is a hole
B is the abbreviation for book, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Someone unsteady on their feet chucks their books into a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk with a limping, unsteady gait is to totter or stagger.

clue.text: Playing footsie with standoffish female? That's futile

indicators.note: toying with, so the letters of the word are moved around
read as 'stand off', so the female letter stands aside from the anagram

explanation.surface: Flirting under the table with an aloof woman is a waste of effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Otiose means serving no purpose, pointless and useless, so it matches futile.
